title: WPSS/1471/2013 of Lalit Kumar Tegwal Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1471 (SS) of 2013
Lalit Kumar Tegwal ÖÖ.ÖPetitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ÖÖ..ÖRespondents
Present: Mr. I.P. Gairola, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
 Mr. T.P.S. Takuli, Brief Holder present for the State/respondent
nos. 1 to 4.
 Mr. Parikshit Saini, Advocate, present for respondent No. 5.
 Mr. Siddhartha Sah, Advocate, present for respondent no.6.

Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioner before this Court has challenged
the selection and appointment of respondent no.6 as
Lecturer (Physics) in grant-in-aid college, namely,
R.M.P.P.V. Inter College, Gurukul Narsan, District-Haridwar.
2. The petitioner has challenged the appointment of
respondent no.6 on the ground that wrong quality points
were awarded to the respondent no.6 points which he never
deserved. In the interview Respondent No.6 has been given
16 marks whereas the petitioner has been awarded only
12.6 marks.
3. Counter affidavits and rejoinder affidavits have
been exchanged and the parties are represented by their
respective counsel.
4. Inter alia, a post of Lecturer (Physics) fell vacant
in Raja Mahendra Pratap Prem Vidyalaya Inter College
(from herein after referred to as ìthe R.M.P.P.V.î), Gurukul
Narsan, District Haridwar and thereafter requisition was
made by the Management Committee to the District
Education Officer, Haridwar for filling up the post. The
advertisement was issued by the Management Committee
for the post of Lecturer (Physics), which was reserved for

the Scheduled Caste category candidates, and pursuant to
the advertisement, eligible candidates applied and the
application forms were submitted in the Office of District
Education Officer, Haridwar and thereafter seven
candidates were shortlisted.
5. Thereafter, the selection committee examined the
documents of all the candidates and awarded marks to
them which included marks for High School, Intermediate,
Graduation, Post Graduation extra curricular activities.
The petitioner has secured 77.7 quality marks whereas
respondent no. 6 has secured 75.36 quality marks. In the
interview, however, the respondent no.6 was given 16
marks whereas the petitioner was given 12.6 marks. Thus,
the total marks obtained by the petitioner is
77.7+12.6=90.3 whereas the total marks obtained by the
respondent no.6 is 75.36 +16 = 91.36, as such, as per the
marks secured, the respondent no.6 was selected and
thereafter he was appointed on the post of lecturer
(physics) in the said institute.
6. The challenge of the petitioner is that wrong
quality marks have been given to the respondent no. 6 for
NSS Certificate. As per the Rules, 5 marks are to be given
to a candidate having certificate in NCC ëCí Certificate/NSS
ëCí Certificate or achievement at the national in sports
activity. Three marks were to be given for participation at
national level sports activity or achievement at the State
level, two marks are given for participation in sports
activity at the State level or achievement at the district
level.
7. In the counter affidavit filed by the State what
has emerged is that five marks have been awarded to
respondent no. 6 for ìNational Social Serviceî (NSS)
Certificate, however, respondent no. 6 has no such

certificate for this activity and in fact there is a clear
averment that the respondent no.6 never participated in
National Social Service and he was not liable to be awarded
five marks for such certificate. The case of the respondents,
however, is that five marks were actually given to the
respondent no.6 for participating in a national level sports
activity.
8. The respondents have annexed a certificate on
the basis of which five marks were awarded to respondent
no.6, which is admitted. This Certificate is of ì4th All India
Gold Cup Super Cricket Championship 2008î in which the
respondent no.6 has participated as a ëplayerí and was
placed runner up.
9. At this juncture, it must be stated that regarding
these appointments at R.M.P.P.V. College complaints were
made to the State authorities. Two inquiries were hence
conducted, one by the education authorities and the other
by the District Magistrate. In both the enquiries it has been
found that marks have been wrongly awarded to private
respondent no.6. In the inquiry report of the education
authorities, it has come that some manipulation has been
with the marks awarded to the respondent no.6.
10. It is true that quality marks can be given for
participation in NSS or for NCC or for achievement in
sports at national level, state level or district level. Even
assuming that respondent no.6 was given five marks for
participating in a national level activity, yet the activity for
which the certificate has been given cannot be called a
ìnational level sports activityî. The Cricket Championship
was organized by a private body for which five marks have
been awarded. It is also true that mere participation in an
event does not amount to an ìachievementî. What goes to
the root of the matter is that such quality marks can only

be given for the sports activity organized either by the
government or sports authority or by an authority
recognized by the government which has a monopoly in
that area, for example ìBoard of Control for Cricket in
Indiaî.
11. In view thereof, five marks awarded to the
respondent no.6 for a cricket activity could not have been
given. This has been given for nothing but apparently for
reasons other than merit. It is clearly wrong.
12. In view of the above facts and circumstances, the
writ petition is allowed. The appointment of the respondent
no.6 being in violation of law is set aside. A mandamus is
issued to the respondents/State authorities to give
appointment to the petitioner, if the petitioner is otherwise
qualified for the post in question, and is next in the merit.
13. No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 30.07.2014
ML
